asked: Feature 435 T02 times every call-cutting hunk's revert (FR-004, plan D6: a claim that an arm's revert cannot be written goes here). One cannot be written against HEAD as its own hunk: 427 T07's hoisted privy reach (hunk 6, removes-work) - feature 427 T12 later folded that code into _first, which takes px(PRIVY_SUN_MAX_FT) once per call, so no per-seat px() remains to restore; restoring the per-seat cost means restoring T12's generator form, which is exactly moves-T12.patch, timed as its own arm. Accept that T07 hunk 6 is timed through moves-T12 (no separate arm), its evidence recorded so?
why: Hunk 6 of 427 T07 lifts the same px(PRIVY_SUN_MAX_FT) call out of the per-seat loop, so it removes work by construction. That is not the trap the GM named, which is moving work around, so if it has no arm of its own the class decision (keep) still holds. The question's claim does not hold up on its own terms, though. T07 came before T12, so the code T12 replaced may already have had the hoist, in which case reverting T12 does not bring back the per-seat px() and nothing about hunk 6 gets timed. The record has to say which case this is, not assume it. PRIVY_SUN_MAX_FT is researched (48 ft, research 0047, IN-STEP), so no packing is involved.
what: Waived: T07 hunk 6 gets no separate perf-ab arm. Read the reverted side of moves-T12.patch and write hunk 6's evidence row as exactly one of two cases. (a) The reverted arm calls px(PRIVY_SUN_MAX_FT) once per seat: then hunk 6's cost comes back and is timed through the moves-T12 arm, and its keep-or-revert follows that arm's decision. (b) The reverted arm calls px once per call: then hunk 6 has no arm and is not timed, and it is kept as removes-work, a loop-invariant hoist whose revert cannot be written against HEAD. Use those words, not 'timed through T12'. Then go on with the remaining candidate groups.

asked: Feature 435 T02 (FR-004, plan D6) timed every call-cutting hunk's revert. Four removes-work arms - removes-T07, removes-T08, removes-T09 (427) and removes-T63 (417 T63's conflicts(first=True)) - cost no measurable time when reverted (within about +-2.7% at 20 and 40 households, inside the spread) and their extra calls are flat from 10 to 40 households, so FR-004's rule reads 'revert'. But their reverts restore per-candidate scans of geometry that does not change during the scan (per-point loops, generators over every house, inside_many rebuilding shapes per call, collector_crossings scanning every segment) and a full conflict collection where admits needs one answer - the shape dev/performance.md names first and constitution X clause 15 forbids ('MUST NOT walk every item on the map per candidate'); and a 4x size range cannot show the GM's scale ('from dozens to hundreds. And then eventually, literally, to thousands'), where removes-T54, the same kind of change, already bends at 4x (its revert's extra calls 4.2% -> 13.2% from 20 to 40). The GM named as the target 'the changes ... that reduced call counts without actually improving performance, because they were done by falling into the exact trap' - moving work; these remove it. Should the four removes-work arms be KEPT (the eight moves-work arms reverted, removes-T54 kept on the size ground), or reverted as the rule reads? (Their patches as written also leave dead helpers that would fail the coverage floor.)
why: FR-004 keeps a group where its time shows a gain OR where how its work grows with size argues for it. The time clause decides nothing here: every arm in the table, these four included, sits inside the runs' spread (HEAD's own 40-household spread is 1.8 s on 18.6 s), which the spec's edge case calls neither a gain nor a loss, and reverting on that reading would gate a revert on a timing, against FR-006. That leaves the growth clause, which is about the shape of the work and not about a 10-40 household sample of a counter that does not see builtins or C. Scans of unchanging geometry repeated per candidate over every house, segment or conflict are the shape constitution X clause 15 forbids and the shape that bends at the GM's hundreds and thousands, so the four arms stand on that clause. Supporting points: the GM's trap is moving work, and these arms remove it; reverting cannot lower time, which is the goal; and the patches as written leave dead helpers that fail the coverage floor.
what: Keep removes-T07, removes-T08, removes-T09 and removes-T63: do not apply their patches. The eight moves-work arms are reverted and removes-T54 is kept, as already decided, with T07 hunk 6 kept under the earlier ruling. In t02-evidence.md, write one line per kept arm naming what its revert would scan per candidate (per point, per clump, per collector segment, per conflict) and what that set grows with (households, grid points, collector segments, conflicts), citing constitution X clause 15. Record the time column as inside the spread for every arm, per the spec's edge case. Carry the four kept arms and this ground into report-numbers.md (FR-008), beside the numbers, so the GM sees the judgment in the report he asked for. Then go on to the three cheap fixes.

asked: Feature 435 FR-005/D7 asks for T57 item 3, the homestead bundle's geometry built once per (form, size, fixtures) and moved into place. Measured 2026-10-27 (make perf-profile SEED=25 STAGE=homesteads HOUSEHOLDS=40, dev/perf-log/20261027T174437Z-profile-adhoc-seed25-homesteads.txt): _bundle_geom 4,506 calls build 2,369 layouts (_bundle_template already caches per key), lay_fixtures 0.68 of the layouts' 0.76 s profiled. The template's key holds the seat the household is offered from because its rolls (yard size, garden jitter, fixture sizes and places, Settlement._hjit at the seat) are per seat; settlement/rolling/place.py:137-140 records that feature 297 (plan C, research R9) TRIED keying them on the household and WITHDREW it: the per-seat rolls were the seating's only way to fit a large-yard household into a tight spot, seed 3 seated 9 of 10 and its site was refused. Dropping the seat from the key is that withdrawn change; keeping it, there is no exact once-built geometry to reuse (the four garden sides each lay their own fixtures). Question: may T03 set item 3 down as not doable as worded (the evidence recorded, the time it would have bought stated: about 0.3 s of an ~8 s roll, the homesteads profile's share in unprofiled time), proceeding with items 1 and 2 (wells, notice), or must a reshaped item 3 be attempted?
why: Item 3 as worded is already in the code as far as the record allows: _bundle_template caches the unraked layout per key and _bundle_geom moves and rakes it per candidate, and the key carries the offered seat because the yard, garden and fixture rolls are per seat; the only further step, dropping the seat, is feature 297's withdrawn change (place.py:137-140, seed 3 seated 9 of 10 and its site refused), which moves maps. The stake is about 0.3 s of an ~8 s roll (0.76 s profiled under cProfile's roughly threefold overhead), which the checklist's 'what it expects to save' question answers: not enough to buy a design change, and a reshaped item 3 (say, fixtures laid lazily for the envelope's four-side probes) is a different change with its own map risk, not a cheap fix, so it is not owed in T03. On packing: the reason the seat stays in the key is itself a packing mechanism - per-seat rerolls of the yard exist to fit a large-yard household into a tight spot - resting on SEATING_GROUND_FT (GUESS, research question owed) and HOMESTEAD_GROUND_FT (UNRESEARCHED), both of which GROW.
what: Go on as proposed: (1) T03 records item 3 as set down, with the profile (dev/perf-log/20261027T174437Z-profile-adhoc-seed25-homesteads.txt), place.py:137-140's withdrawn change, and the ~0.3 s it would have bought; (2) amend spec.md so FR-005 and SC-004 read the cheap fixes as items 2 and 1 built and item 3 measured and set down, citing this ruling (ask:435-bundle-once), so spec-fidelity does not re-open it; (3) proceed with items 2 (notice) and 1 (wells); (4) the closing report (FR-008) states item 3 not built and why, and lists two next-step candidates: fixtures laid only for the side and seat chosen rather than every envelope probe, and a roomier seating band (SEATING_GROUND_FT first) that may remove the need for per-seat rerolls and so reopen a per-household template key; (5) file one row: _bundle_geom's docstring says the layout is 'built once per household and size' while the cache is per offered seat (2,369 layouts for 40 households), the overstatement that led T57 to rank item 3 an S at ~0.5M - correct the docstring so the next analysis does not re-rank it.
